## Clinical History

A 56-year-old man with a rising prostate-specific antigen of 8.4 ng/mL and an abnormal digital rectal examination. Targeted and systematic transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsies were submitted from twelve sites for histological assessment.

## Gross Description

Received in twelve formalin-filled containers, each labelled with the sextant site. Cores range from 9 to 17 mm in length and are entirely submitted. Containers are processed separately and embedded in numbered cassettes.

## Microscopic Description

Sections show prostatic adenocarcinoma involving four of twelve cores, all on the right side. The tumour shows fused and poorly formed glands consistent with Gleason pattern 4 admixed with well-formed pattern 3 glands. No perineural invasion is identified. Benign cores show foci of high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia.

## Diagnosis

- **Prostate, biopsy:** Acinar adenocarcinoma, Gleason score 3+4=7 (Grade Group 2).
- **Tumour extent:** 4 of 12 cores positive; greatest core involvement 40%.
- **Recommendation:** Correlate with imaging; discuss at urology multidisciplinary meeting.
